title: AgentFirstStack: analytics, tag manager, email and session replay your AI agent sets up
excerpt: Analytics, tag management, email inboxes and session replay your AI agent sets up end to end. No signup form. Free and open source.
content_html:
Like Google Analytics, Google Tag Manager and Hotjar, plus email inboxes your agent can use. Paste one prompt and your coding agent creates the account, adds everything to your site and checks it works. No signup form, no dashboard. Free and open source.

Paste it into Claude Code, Cursor, Codex or any agent that can make HTTP requests.

How it works

  1. Paste one prompt

    It tells your agent where the manual is. Nothing to configure, and no account to create first.

  2. Your agent does the setup

    One request gets a key that works on every service. No email, password or verification. The agent installs, verifies and fixes as it goes.

  3. You approve what only you can

    Your ad accounts stay yours. The agent asks for the exact IDs and tokens it needs from Google Ads, Meta or TikTok, and tells you where to find them. It also gives you a link to claim the project, so you can see everything in a dashboard.

Four services, one key

Each has a REST API, an MCP server and a plain-text manual.

Analytics instead of Google Analytics

See where every visitor comes from

  • United Kingdom14%

  • Goals and revenue
  • No cookies
Add analytics with Claude Code

Count every conversion once

  • Meta200 OK

What each service includes

All of it over REST and MCP, with the same key. Comparisons with the tools you may use now.

Analytics instead of GA4, Plausible or DataFast

Tracking
Cookieless by default, single-page and hash routing, custom events and properties (also from HTML attributes), outbound clicks, downloads, forms, 404s, scroll depth, engaged time, Core Web Vitals, site search, UTMs and ad click IDs, consent gating, cross-domain linking

Server events
An events API with a dry run, joined to browser visitors, with user properties

Reports
Stats, timeseries and comparisons, breakdowns by up to three dimensions, custom metrics, channel groups, realtime with a map, engagement rate, average order value, top movers, insights, CSV, one rollup across all your sites

Filters
Wildcards, nested and/or groups, saved segments, new or returning, did or didn't do an event, user properties, timezones

Goals and funnels
Goals that apply to past data, funnels in order or any order, with time windows and revenue per step

People
Visitors, a session list linked to replay, journeys, first touch, retention cohorts, path exploration, six attribution models

Revenue
Stripe in one call with 90 days of history, Polar, Paddle and LemonSqueezy, a payments API, one reporting currency, new and renewal revenue by source, page and campaign

Subscriptions
MRR, ARR and ARPU; new, expansion, contraction and churned MRR; churn and trial conversion, by channel, campaign, country or plan

Ad spend
Import costs per campaign for ROAS, CPA and CAC

Ecommerce
Items in each purchase, with revenue and quantity per product

AI crawlers
Which AI bots read which pages, never counted as visitors

Querying
Read-only SQL with cost limits, and a schema call that lists every event and property

Import and export
GA4 and Plausible CSV imports, raw events as NDJSON, CSV or JSON

Sharing
Public dashboards with a password, an expiry and a saved segment

Alerts
Spikes, drops, no data, goals and payments, plus weekly or monthly reports, by webhook, Slack or email

Privacy
Delete a visitor, purge with a dry run, email and phone redaction, path rules, exclusions, a referral-spam filter, Do Not Track and GPC

Tags instead of Google Tag Manager

Workflow
A draft you edit item by item, diffs between versions, GTM import, a preview log, environments, versions and rollback

Triggers
Pageview, DOM ready, window loaded, consent initialization, clicks, forms, history changes, element visibility, scroll depth, timers, JavaScript errors, video, custom events, trigger groups

Variables
Data layer, URL parts, cookies, element attributes, lookup and regex tables, formatting, about 30 built-ins

Tag options
Priority, scheduling, sequencing, firing limits, consent per tag

Browser tags
GA4, Google Ads, Meta, TikTok, Snap, image pixels, custom HTML on verified domains

Conversion APIs
GA4, Google Ads, Meta, TikTok, LinkedIn, Pinterest, Reddit, Snap, X and webhooks, each counted once with the browser pixel

Routing
Per-platform conditions and parameter rules, test sends

Consent and identity
Consent Mode v2, TCF v2, hashed user data, cross-domain linking, a lookup store for values like margin by SKU

Monitoring
An event and delivery log, tag-fire stats, page coverage, retries and a circuit breaker

Mail instead of AgentMail or a Gmail account

Inboxes
Instant inboxes on our domain or yours, plus-address tags, labels, usage limits you can read

Waiting
Wait for an email and get the verification code or link back, from authenticated senders only

Reading
Threads, search, raw email, attachments and their text, calendar invites, replies without the quoted history

Sending
Send, reply and forward, safe to retry, scheduled sending, delivery status per recipient

Safety
Inboxes on the shared domain reply only to people who wrote first; allow and block lists

Domains
Custom domains with DNS checks, send-only domains, a zone file to import

Events
Signed webhooks, and an event feed an agent can poll without a public URL

Checks
A deliverability report for any message: SPF, DKIM and DMARC

Replay instead of Hotjar or Clarity

Recording
Text and inputs masked in the browser by default, selectors to unmask, mask or block, sampling

Consent
Consent only where the law asks (EEA, UK, Switzerland), Google Consent Mode, TCF v2, Do Not Track and GPC, IP exclusion

Sessions
Search, readable transcripts, summaries across many sessions, raw events, exports, a share-link player and clips

Signals
Rage, dead and error clicks, quick backs, excessive scrolling, JavaScript and console errors, failed requests, a frustration score

Analysis
Tags and identify, saved segments, trends, funnel drop-offs, events defined after the fact

Heatmaps
Click, scroll and attention maps by element or zone, comparisons, conversion share, PNG images

Surveys
Popovers, embedded surveys and a feedback tab: NPS, CSAT, CES, product-market fit and text, triggered on exit intent or after a rage click, each answer linked to its session

Workflow
Notes, labels, stars, signed webhooks, signals sent on to analytics and your tag container

Privacy
Delete or look up one visitor's data, recordings kept 14 days

Server-side by default

Conversions go from your site and your backend to each ad platform's conversion API, using your own credentials. Ad blockers and short-lived browser cookies don't lose them.

Your siteone snippet, or served from your own domain

Your backendpurchases and sign-ups from Stripe or your API

AgentFirstStack keeps click IDs, dedupes, retries, logs each platform's answer

Google Ads

Meta

GA4

TikTok

Built for agents, not dashboards

One request to an account

No email, captcha or approval. The key is the account.

API and MCP for everything

Nothing hides behind a settings page.

A manual in plain text

/llms.txt lists every endpoint, tool and field.

Every step can be checked

The agent verifies its own work instead of guessing.

Safe to retry

Creating the same thing twice returns the first one.

Errors that explain the fix

Each one carries a hint the agent can act on.

Free to use. Open source.

Hosted

  • 3 new accounts per hour from one network
  • 10 sites, 10 tag containers and 10 inboxes per account; 5 replay sites
  • Shared inboxes reply to people who wrote to them, up to 20 recipients a day. Add your own domain to send to anyone.
  • Mail on shared addresses is kept for 14 days, up to 100 messages per inbox
  • Replay keeps recordings for up to 14 days, 200 sessions per site a day

Self-host

Open source under AGPL-3.0 (the scripts your pages load are MIT). Four commands deploy it to your own Cloudflare account.

git clone https://github.com/StartGlobal-AI/agentfirststack
cd agentfirststack && pnpm install
pnpm afs init mystack --domain example.com --account <id>
pnpm afs deploy mystack

content_html_zh:
Like Google Analytics, Google Tag Manager and Hotjar, plus email inboxes your agent can use. Paste one prompt and your coding agent creates the account, adds everything to your site and checks it works. No signup form, no dashboard. 免费且开源。

Paste it into Claude Code, Cursor, Codex or any agent that can make HTTP requests.

它是如何运作的

  1. Paste one prompt It tells your agent where the manual is. Nothing to configure, and no account to create first.
  2. Your agent does the setup One request gets a key that works on every service. No email, password or verification. The agent installs, verifies and fixes as it goes.
  3. You approve what only you can Your ad accounts stay yours. The agent asks for the exact IDs and tokens it needs from Google Ads, Meta or TikTok, and tells you where to find them. It also gives you a link to claim the project, so you can see everything in a dashboard.

Four services, one key

Each has a REST API, an MCP server and a plain-text manual.

  • 3 new accounts per hour from one network
  • 10 sites, 10 tag containers and 10 inboxes per account; 5 replay sites
  • Shared inboxes reply to people who wrote to them, up to 20 recipients a day. Add your own domain to send to anyone.

Open source under AGPL-3.0 (the scripts your pages load are MIT). Four commands deploy it to your own Cloudflare account.
